data.title: Cambridge Savings adds a digital stalwart to its board
data.description:
• Supporting data: Cambridge Savings’ five-year-old online-only Ivy Bank subsidiary has grown to $1.3 billion of deposits. 
  • Expert quote:  “Once you’ve built a brand and gained a customer base, you can build on that. There’re fewer examples of banks that have done that well.” —Cambridge Savings Bank director John Rosenfeld

John Rosenfeld left Sumitomo Mitsui Banking in March, after helping wind down its Jenius digital-bank division.

data.title: Trump signs Common Cents Act, setting rules for post-penny era
data.description:
• Key insight: The new law serves less to end the minting of pennies, which stopped more than a year ago, than to establish clear guidelines and legal protection for rounding prices.
  • Expert quote: “This bipartisan legislation provides clarity on cash rounding, reduces unnecessary costs and helps ensure a smooth transition away from the penny.” —the American Bankers Association

In practical terms, the U.S. penny died more than a year ago. Now President Trump has signed legislation to make its death as painless as possible for banks and retailers.

data.title: How data center backlash could put banks’ AI bets under pressure
data.description:
• Key insight: Local opposition to data-center construction could threaten lending and underwriting business for banks, particularly for projects still awaiting permits or approval.
  • Forward look: Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., is pushing for greater disclosure of AI-related financing, a proposal with bipartisan support that could gain traction in the next Congress.

WASHINGTON — Along with the election cycle’s blue wave that’s shifting power on Capitol Hill, voters also delivered a sweeping rebuke to artificial intelligence and a data center buildout that fueled many grassroots movements across the country.

data.title: Banks plan move from blocking AI agents to working with them
data.description:
Key insight: U.S. banks have defaulted to blocking external AI agents, but recognize they need to create the right protocols to work with them, including “know your agent” processes.

Expert quote: “If you think philosophically about the way we operate today, the goal is to exclude bots,” said Jackie Reses, CEO and co-founder of Lead Bank. “It’s ironic because we are now in a world where machines are operating at scale and in excess numbers to humans, and so we’ve completely turned on its head the idea that we are now engaging with machines versus humans. Our goal is to now enable machines to access, manage, control a lot of the components of the financial system, albeit with human-directed interaction. It’s fascinating.”

data.title: Banks should reconsider putting AI agent liability on consumers
data.description:
Key Insights: AI agents are gaining the ability to initiate payments and execute trades, while major U.S. banks are hitting the brakes over concerns about security even as tech rivals race forward. 

Forward look: As tech giants embed themselves deeper into the payment experience, banks will have to balance risk controls against customer retention.

data.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO with government input
data.description:
(Bloomberg) —

Nvidia Corp.’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer, effective immediately. Nvidia gained more than 27% on the news.

data.title: Press Release Vstock Transfer Expands Its Issuer Services Platform with Issuer-Sponsored Tokenized Shares Through a Strategic Collaboration with Metagood
data.description:
New York, United States, November 23rd, 2026, FinanceWire


Public companies and companies preparing to go public will have a single agent for shareholder records, corporate actions and tokenized ownership as the SEC’s Innovation Exemption opens U.S. markets to onchain trading

Vstock Transfer, LLC (“Vstock”), an SEC-registered transfer agent and registrar serving approximately 1,000 issuers, including companies listed on the NYSE, Nasdaq and OTC Markets, today announced a strategic collaboration with Metagood, a tokenization and lifecycle management provider for regulated digital assets, under which it plans to add issuer-sponsored tokenized shares to its suite of issuer services.

Through the collaboration, Vstock will offer public companies and companies preparing to go public the ability to issue their shares in token form, supported by the same team that manages their shareholder records, corporate actions and annual meetings. Metagood’s patent-pending platform will connect directly to Vstock’s recordkeeping system, so token holders and book-entry holders will appear on a single shareholder register, and dividends, stock splits, tender offers and shareholder votes will be processed once for every holder.

The tokens will be the company’s own shares, recorded in token form by its transfer agent. They will not be wrappers, derivatives or synthetic products. They are designed so that a token holder is a registered shareholder with the same economic and voting rights as a holder of book-entry shares. The platform is interoperable across multiple blockchains and built to add more, so an issuer’s shares can be offered on the networks its investors use.

Tokenized shares will be the latest addition to Vstock’s expanding suite of services, which spans shareholder recordkeeping, DTC eligibility and DWAC transfers, corporate actions, proxy and annual meeting services, IPO and SPAC support, and equity administration. Vstock continues to build its platform around one principle: anticipating what issuers will need next and delivering it with the responsiveness required of the capital markets.

A Governance Decision, Not Just a Technology Decision

For boards and management teams, tokenization is now a governance question as much as a technology question. Sponsoring tokenized shares through their transfer agent gives companies a way to participate on their own terms, with their official register, their shareholder relationships and their corporate actions intact.

“Companies come to us for guidance well before they come to us for a service, and tokenization is now at the top of the list,” said Yoel Goldfeder, Chief Executive Officer of Vstock Transfer. “Issuers want to know how they can offer their shares in token form, and how to do it on their own terms. This collaboration gives them a clear path. We selected Metagood because its platform was built for what a transfer agent does every day after shares are issued: paying dividends, processing corporate actions and counting every vote accurately.”

“We built our first tokenization product at Vstock years ago, and we learned that the market was not ready for it,” said Seth Farbman, Chairman and Founder of Vstock Transfer. “The rules, the exchanges and investor demand have now caught up, and small and mid-cap companies deserve access to the same tools as the largest issuers. For a growth company CEO, tokenized shares can open the door to a new generation of investors and a more direct relationship with shareholders. Whether a company is preparing for its IPO, planning an uplisting or simply evaluating its options, we want Vstock to be its first call.”

Danny Yang, Chief Executive Officer of Metagood, commented, “Our platform will let Vstock handle every dividend, vote and corporate action for token holders with the same precision it delivers for book-entry holders today.”

Companies interested in issuer-sponsored tokenized shares, or in learning more about third-party tokenization notices under the Innovation Exemption, are invited to schedule a consultation with the Vstock team at info@vstocktransfer.com or visit www.vstocktransfer.com.

About Vstock Transfer

Vstock Transfer, LLC is an SEC-registered stock transfer agent and registrar serving approximately 1,000 issuers, from private companies and IPOs to public companies listed on the NYSE, NYSE American, Nasdaq and OTC Markets. Founded and managed by securities attorneys, Vstock provides shareholder recordkeeping, certificate services, DTC eligibility and DWAC transfers, proxy and annual meeting services, and equity administration tools. Vstock is based in New York.

For more information, visit www.vstocktransfer.com

About Metagood

Metagood provides next generation infrastructure for regulated financial assets. Its patent-pending platform connects traditional financial systems with blockchain networks to tokenize assets and automate their lifecycle, including transfers, payments, distributions and corporate actions. Built for financial institutions, transfer agents, exchanges and issuers, Metagood enables securities, mortgages and other regulated assets to be managed more efficiently and transparently across traditional and digital markets.

For more information, visit www.metagood.com



Contact
Yoel Goldfeder
info@vstocktransfer.com

data.title: Press Release Nocera Signs Binding Letter of Intent to Invest $22 Million for an Approximately 44% Stake in BitRock, a Self-Powered AI Data Center Developer in Alberta
data.description:
Taipei, Taiwan, November 23rd, 2026, FinanceWire


First 10 MW Facility on BitRock’s Own Natural Gas Power Extends the AI Platform Nocera Is Building Through Its IRMA AI, INERGX and QMAX Agreements

Nocera, Inc. (Nasdaq: NCRA) (“Nocera” or the “Company”) today announced that it has entered into a binding letter of intent (the “LOI”) with BitRock Ltd. (“BitRock”), a Calgary-based developer of AI data centers powered by its own natural gas generation, to invest approximately US$22 million in cash for newly issued BitRock shares. At a post-money valuation of approximately US$50 million, the investment would give Nocera approximately 44% of BitRock, together with the right to appoint directors and to take part in decisions on major matters. The proceeds are dedicated solely to building BitRock’s first AI data center, a facility of approximately 10 MW of IT load in Alberta, Canada.

The LOI, fully executed on November 19, 2026, is legally binding, and the parties have committed to execute a definitive investment agreement as soon as practicable. Nocera’s obligation to fund is subject to completion of due diligence, execution of the definitive agreement, receipt of required approvals and other conditions, and the investment may not be completed on the terms described or at all.

Power First

Nocera believes the limit on new AI capacity in North America is no longer demand. It is power: grid connections that can take years to secure and approvals that have become harder to win. BitRock starts from the other end. Under the LOI, BitRock has represented that it owns its natural gas generation equipment and has obtained the permits required to generate and supply electricity in Alberta, and its first facility is planned around that generation. According to BitRock, it already holds its power generation, power supply and usage permits, and its future expansion will also be based mainly on self-generated power from natural gas.

Why Alberta

Alberta launched its AI Data Centres Strategy in December 2024 with a stated goal of attracting C$100 billion of data center investment over five years. According to public reports, the Alberta Electric System Operator has since fully allocated its interim 1,200 MW of grid capacity for large-load projects, and provincial policy now favors developers that bring their own generation. Nocera believes BitRock is built on that model.

Built in 10 MW Steps

According to BitRock, its planned campus is located near Hanna, Alberta, on an industrial site of approximately 37 acres, and uses prefabricated computing modules of approximately 2.5 MW each, with four modules making up the first 10 MW phase. BitRock’s long-term plan for the campus is approximately 200 MW, added in 10 MW units as customer demand warrants. This investment covers the first phase; each further phase would be evaluated and financed on its own merits.

According to BitRock, the campus is designed to a power usage effectiveness (PUE) target of approximately 1.225, with N+1 redundancy and uninterruptible power supply supporting stable operation of the compute load. Alberta’s cold climate is expected to reduce the energy and water needed for cooling.

BitRock plans to operate on a colocation model in which customers install their own computing equipment and BitRock provides powered data hall space and operations. Under that model, Nocera’s capital goes into power and data center capacity rather than chips. BitRock has represented that customers have signed memoranda of understanding for computing power hosting services.

“Power is the scarce asset in AI infrastructure, and BitRock is built around its own,” said Andrew Teng, Asia Director of Nocera. “We are putting capital into a facility designed to generate its own electricity, in a province that has asked developers to do exactly that, and we are doing it one 10 megawatt unit at a time. This is a measured entry into North American compute with a meaningful ownership position and a voice on the board.”

One AI Strategy, Four Layers

BitRock is the fourth piece of an AI platform Nocera has been assembling since June. On June 8, 2026, Nocera entered into a binding venture platform agreement with U.S.-based Digital Innovations Group, developer of the proprietary IRMA AI Engine, to pair IRMA’s AI technology with Nocera’s capital markets and acquisition platform. That transaction has not yet closed, as Digital Innovations Group is in the midst of a major expansion across the Asia Pacific region, and Nocera expects it to close before the end of 2026. On July 8, Nocera announced a binding agreement to acquire an equity interest in INERGX, an integrated energy storage and power platform built to serve AI data centers and other mission-critical users, and followed in August with a 50/50 joint venture, Nocera-INERGX Energy Ventures. On July 29, Nocera announced the acquisition of a 30% controlling interest in QMAX Technology Co., Ltd., a Taiwan-based authorized distributor of Micron / Crucial memory and storage products.

AI software, power, memory and now self-powered data center capacity: Nocera believes each transaction adds a layer of the infrastructure that artificial intelligence depends on. Certain of these transactions, including the BitRock investment and the Digital Innovations Group transaction, have not yet closed and remain subject to conditions.

Transaction Terms

  • Investment: approximately US$22 million in cash for newly issued shares, on a pre-money valuation of approximately US$28 million, which reflects BitRock’s generation equipment, generation permits and land use rights, and a post-money valuation of approximately US$50 million, for approximately 44% of BitRock.
  • Use of proceeds: solely for construction of the first data center of approximately 10 MW. Instalments and disbursement conditions will be set in the definitive agreement.
  • Governance: as a shareholder, Nocera will have the right to appoint directors, receive periodic financial reports and participate in decisions on major matters. BitRock is responsible for construction management and day-to-day operations.
  • Conditions to funding: due diligence reasonably satisfactory to Nocera, execution of the definitive agreement, required corporate and regulatory approvals, accuracy of the information provided by BitRock and no material adverse change at BitRock.
  • Valuation protection: if due diligence results differ materially from the information BitRock has provided, the pre-money valuation will be adjusted, and either party may call for an independent valuation.
  • Term: 60 days from signing, extendable by 30 days by mutual written consent while due diligence continues. The agreement is non-exclusive. 

About BitRock Ltd.

BitRock Ltd. is a corporation organized under the laws of the Province of Alberta, Canada, with its registered office in Calgary, focused on the development and operation of AI data centers powered by self-generated natural gas.

About Nocera, Inc.

Nocera, Inc. (Nasdaq: NCRA) is building a portfolio of AI and energy infrastructure businesses across Asia, Europe and North America, spanning AI model aggregation and distribution, data center and compute assets, device and channel operations, and renewable energy and storage assets. For more information, visit www.Nocera.company. For AI partnership inquiries, contact AI@PhoenixMGMTConsulting.com.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding the Company’s proposed investment in BitRock, the resulting ownership interest and governance rights, the construction, capacity, timing and expansion of BitRock’s data center, BitRock’s business model and customers, and the Company’s AI and energy infrastructure strategy. The approximately 200 MW campus plan is BitRock’s long-term objective, not a commitment; this investment concerns only the first phase of approximately 10 MW. Such statements involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties, including that: Nocera is not obligated to fund the investment unless a definitive investment agreement is signed and all conditions are satisfied, including due diligence reasonably satisfactory to Nocera; the definitive agreement may not be signed on the terms described or at all; the LOI has a 60-day term and may expire or be terminated; the valuation, investment amount and ownership percentage may be adjusted; Nocera will require sufficient capital to complete the investment and has not yet secured financing for it; customer memoranda of understanding may not result in binding contracts; construction may face delays, cost overruns and equipment, fuel price, tariff and regulatory risks; the Digital Innovations Group transaction has not closed and may not close by the end of 2026, on the terms announced or at all; and the other earlier transactions referenced above remain subject to their own terms, conditions and risks. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied. Nocera undertakes no obligation to update any forward-looking statement except as required by law. Statements concerning BitRock’s generation equipment, permits, site, technical design, customers and expansion plans are based on information provided by BitRock and have not yet been independently verified by Nocera. Nothing in this release constitutes an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any security.

data.title: BankThink The US needs more banks; we should streamline the chartering process
data.description:
• Supporting data: The top five largest banks in the U.S. went from 29% market share in 2007 to 38% market share in 2025. This makes a system dangerously fragile, reliant on a few institutions that are simply too big to fail.
  • Forward look: Coming into the 120th Congress, members of the House and the Senate have a remarkable opportunity to clear the path for more de novo banks.

On Nov. 3, voters on both sides of the aisle named the economy as their top issue. Seven in 10 said the economic system favors the wealthy. When the new Congress begins, Democrats and Republicans have a chance to deliver an economy that works for more Americans by renewing America’s once firm commitment to establishing more full-service, insured banks. These banks are uniquely positioned to fund job creation in their sectors of focus and reduce the risk of future bank bailouts.

data.title: Stability concerns have Fed considering dormant capital rule
data.description:
• Key insight: Some Federal Reserve officials are discussing the merits of activating the countercyclical capital buffer — which raises bank capital during the upswing of a business cycle to bolster the banking system during the downswing — for the first time in years. 
  • Expert quote: “The Fed policy framework sets the standard for deploying the countercyclical capital buffer as a period when systemic vulnerabilities are meaningfully above normal. It’s pretty clear that current conditions meet that criteria.” — Jeremy Kress, University of Michigan law professor and former Fed lawyer.

Rising financial stability concerns have some members of the Federal Open Market Committee eying a heretofore unused Federal Reserve regulatory tool.

data.title: How Block is pushing its AI to merchants
data.description:
• Key insights: Block’s merchant payments unit Square launched Squaremates, a business agent that can perform tasks for Square sellers. 
  • What’s at stake: Jack Dorsey’s payments company spent the better part of the last year using artificial intelligence to reimagine how it operates. Now, Block is pushing some of that technology to merchants. 

After more than a year of using artificial intelligence to reshape — and downsize — its organization, Block is providing its sellers with that same technology it hopes will help merchants run their businesses more efficiently.

data.title: Anthropic’s business model is creating a new kind of debt — comprehension debt
data.description:
Dario Amodei, the CEO of newly public Anthropic, said something extraordinary the other day. In explaining what he calls “pacing” in terms of developing the company’s products, he used the metaphor of a car that could drive 200 miles an hour. “We could drive at 200 miles an hour, maybe let’s only drive at 90 miles an hour.”

In other words, the company could develop its products at break-neck speed and release them, but Anthropic has chosen not to do that. Amodei was presenting this as an example of the elevated reasoning at the company.

data.title: Why insurtech unicorn Corgi wants a traditional bank charter
data.description:
• Key insight: Corgi, an insurtech founded two years ago with a focus on AI insurance, has requested a national bank charter in a first for insurers since the Dodd-Frank Act.
  • Expert quote: “Regulators will probe how the firm uses AI and whether it is well-controlled.” -Klaros Group’s Roman Goldstein

AI-powered insurtech startup Corgi is sniffing out a path to a full-service bank charter.

data.title: Costs of running branches in big cities vary widely: Report
data.description:
• Key insight: Location and market conditions largely determine the cost of operating a bank branch, and the difference between certain markets is large, according to a report from JLL, a commercial real estate and investment management firm that manages bank properties.
  • Supporting data: It costs 2.6 times as much money to operate a branch in New York City than it does in Orange County, California, according to JLL’s analysis of 12 U.S. markets.

data.title: Why referrals are bank-based advisors’ best friends and worst enemies
data.description:
• Key insight: Advisors often view the bank channel as a steady source of client referrals. But that source of business has started drying up even as the chances that they’ll be sued if they leave remain strong.
  • Expert quote: “Those customers, they typically have a much much tighter relationship with the bank than they will an FA that’s been assigned to them.” — Ron Edde, founder of Millennium Career Advisors

The very reasons some financial advisors choose to anchor their careers in the bank channel is, perhaps counterintuitively, their biggest impediment to eventually leaving, according to industry data.

data.title: Federal Home Loan bank lending surged 15% in third quarter
data.description:
• Key insight: Third-quarter advances from the Federal Home Loan banks rose 15% to $798.4 million as banks, credit unions and insurers sought liquidity amid higher interest rates. 
  • What’s at stake: With Treasury yields above 5% and deposits moving toward higher-yielding money-market funds, commercial banks continue to tap the Home Loan Bank System to maintain liquidity without broadly repricing deposits.

data.title: TruStage struck a deal with its attacker. What did it buy?
data.description:
• Key insight: TruStage disclosed Thursday that it “came to a resolution” with the attacker behind the July cyberattack on its systems. The attacker promised to destroy any data it took.
  • What’s at stake: Any credit union member data the attacker took is now protected chiefly by a criminal’s promise, and credit unions can’t tell members or regulators anything definitive until TruStage finishes its investigation.
